sentences.zh: __FORCETOC__崔融崔融，字安成，齊州全節人。

translations.literal: __FORCETOC__Cui Rong — Cui Rong, style name Ancheng, was a man of Quanjie in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: __FORCETOC__Cui Rong, whose style name was Ancheng, was a native of Quanjie in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 擢八科高第。

translations.literal: He was selected with high marks in the Eight Subjects examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Eight Subjects examination with top honors.

sentences.zh: 累補宮門丞、崇文館學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Palace Gate Vice-Director and Scholar of the Chongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts as vice-director of the palace gates and scholar of the Chongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 中宗為太子時，選侍讀，典東朝章疏。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was crown prince, Rong was chosen as lecturing attendant and managed memorials of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhongzong was still crown prince, Rong was selected as a lecturing attendant and oversaw memorials for the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 武后幸嵩高，見融銘《啟母碣》，歎美之。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu visited Mount Song, she saw Rong's inscription on the Qi Mother stele and sighed in praise.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu visited Mount Song, she read Rong's inscription on the Qi Mother stele and praised it warmly.

sentences.zh: 及已封，即命銘《朝覲碑》。

translations.literal: When she had already been enfeoffed, she immediately ordered him to inscribe the Court Audience stele.
translations.idiomatic: Once her enfeoffment was complete, she at once commissioned him to compose the Court Audience stele.

sentences.zh: 授著作佐郎，遷右史，進鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Compiler, promoted to Right Historian, and advanced to Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was made assistant compiler, then promoted to right historiographer and advanced to attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 時有司議關市，行人盡征之，融上疏謂：「《周官》九賦，其七曰關市。

translations.literal: At the time the relevant offices debated market tolls at passes, taxing all travelers in full. Rong submitted a memorial saying: "In the Offices of Zhou, among the nine levies, the seventh is called market tolls at passes.
translations.idiomatic: When officials proposed levying market tolls at the passes on all travelers without exception, Rong submitted a memorial arguing: "The Offices of Zhou lists nine levies; the seventh is the pass-market levy.

sentences.zh: 以市多淫巧，而關通末遊，欲止抑之，故加稅耳。

translations.literal: Because markets had many extravagant crafts and passes connected with marginal pursuits, they wished to stop and restrain them, hence the added tax only.
translations.idiomatic: That levy was meant to curb extravagant goods in the markets and the petty traffic that passed through the passes—not to tax ordinary travelers as well.

sentences.zh: 然唯斂工商，而不及往來。

translations.literal: Yet it only collected from artisans and merchants, and did not extend to those coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: It was imposed only on artisans and merchants, not on people merely passing through.

sentences.zh: 今一切通取，則事不師古。

translations.literal: Now to take from all without distinction is a matter that does not follow antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: To levy it on everyone indiscriminately would abandon the precedent of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 且四人異業舊矣，復動而搖之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the four classes with their different occupations is an old arrangement; to stir them again is to shake them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the four classes of society have long had their separate callings; to disturb them again would unsettle the whole order.

sentences.zh: 市者，兼受善惡也。

translations.literal: Markets receive both good and bad together.
translations.idiomatic: Markets accommodate both the worthy and the base alike.

sentences.zh: 若甚，則細人無所容，細人無所容，久必為亂。

translations.literal: If it is excessive, then petty men have nowhere to lodge; if petty men have nowhere to lodge, in time there will surely be disorder.
translations.idiomatic: If the burden is too heavy, the humble will have no room to survive; and when the humble have no room to survive, disorder will follow before long.

sentences.zh: 天下之關必險道，市必要津，豪宗、惡少在焉，聞一旦變法，或致騷動，恐南走蠻，北走狄。

translations.literal: Passes throughout the realm lie on perilous routes, and markets stand at essential fords. Powerful clans and vicious youths dwell there. Hearing that the law changes overnight, they may cause disturbances; I fear they will flee south to the barbarians or north to the Di.
translations.idiomatic: The empire's passes lie on dangerous roads and its markets at vital crossings, where powerful clans and rowdy youths gather. News of a sudden change in the law could spark unrest, driving people south toward the barbarians or north toward the Di.

sentences.zh: 今江津、河滸列鋪率稅，檢覆稽留，加主司僦略邀丐，則商人廢業。

translations.literal: Now at river crossings and river banks stations are set up to levy taxes at a fixed rate; inspection and review cause delays, and when chief officials extort and beg, merchants abandon their trades.
translations.idiomatic: Already at river crossings and along the banks, tax stations levy fixed rates, inspections cause long delays, and supervising officials extort and beg for bribes until merchants abandon their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉、齊、隋所不行，況陛下乎？

translations.literal: What Wei, Jin, Qi, and Sui did not carry out—how much less should Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Even Wei, Jin, Qi, and Sui did not adopt such measures—how much less should Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 有如師興費廣，雖倍算商旅、加斂齊人可也。」

translations.literal: If troops are raised and expenses are vast, then even doubling the levy on traveling merchants and adding collections from the people of Qi would be acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: If armies must be raised and costs mount, then even doubling the levy on traveling merchants and imposing extra taxes on the people of Qi would be justified."

sentences.zh: 後納之。

translations.literal: Later it was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court later accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 張易之兄弟頗延文學士，融與李嶠、蘇味道、麟台少監王紹宗降節佞附。

translations.literal: The Zhang Yizhi brothers greatly drew in literary scholars; Rong, together with Li Jiao, Su Weidao, and Wang Shaozong, Vice-Director of the Lin Terrace, lowered their dignity and fawned in attachment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yizhi and his brothers cultivated literary men, and Rong joined Li Jiao, Su Weidao, and Wang Shaozong, vice-director of the Lin Terrace, in abasing themselves to flatter and attach to them.

sentences.zh: 易之誅，貶袁州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yizhi was executed, Rong was demoted to prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizhi was executed, Rong was demoted to prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 召授國子司業。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice-Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed vice-director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 與脩《武后實錄》勞，封清河縣子。

translations.literal: For labor in compiling the Veritable Records of Empress Wu, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: For his work compiling the Veritable Records of Empress Wu, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 融為文華婉，當時未有輩者。

translations.literal: Rong's writing was florid and graceful; at the time there was no one of his generation.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's prose was ornate and graceful, and in his day he had no peer.

sentences.zh: 朝廷大筆，多手敕委之，其《洛出寶圖頌》尤工。

translations.literal: For great brushwork of the court, many hand-edicts were entrusted to him; his "Eulogy on the Precious Diagram Emerging from the Luo" was especially accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Major state compositions were often entrusted to him by imperial edict, and his "Eulogy on the Precious Diagram Emerging from the Luo" was especially masterful.

sentences.zh: 譔《武后哀冊》最高麗，絕筆而死，時謂思苦神竭雲。

translations.literal: When he composed the Lament for Empress Wu, it was most lofty and refined; he laid down the brush and died. At the time they said his thought had been bitter and his spirit exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: While composing the Lament for Empress Wu—his most exalted work—he set down his brush and died; contemporaries said he had worn out mind and spirit in the effort.

sentences.zh: 年五十四。

translations.literal: He was fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-four years old.

sentences.zh: 贈衛州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Prefect of Weizhou, with posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed prefect of Weizhou, with the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 膳部員外郎杜審言為融所獎引，為服緦麻。

translations.literal: Du Shenyan, Vice-Director of the Board of Provisions, had been encouraged and brought forward by Rong; he wore the three-month mourning garment for him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shenyan, vice-director of the Board of Provisions, whom Rong had mentored, wore three-month mourning for him.

sentences.zh: 六子，其聞者禹錫、翹。

translations.literal: He had six sons; those known were Yuxi and Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons; those of note were Yuxi and Qiao.

sentences.zh: 禹錫，開元中，中書舍人，贈定州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Yuxi, in the Kaiyuan era, was Attendant of the Secretariat; posthumously made Prefect of Dingzhou, with posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxi served as secretariat attendant under Kaiyuan and was posthumously made prefect of Dingzhou, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 翹，禮部尚書，贈荊州大都督，諡曰成。

translations.literal: Qiao was Minister of Rites; posthumously made Grand Protector-General of Jingzhou, with posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao rose to minister of rites and was posthumously made grand protector-general of Jingzhou, with the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 孫巨，右補闕，亦有文。

translations.literal: His grandson Ju was Right Remonstrator and also had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Ju served as right remonstrator and was likewise accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 從曾孫從。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Cong — the great-grandson Cong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson was Cong.

sentences.zh: 從字子乂，少孤貧，與兄能偕隱太原山中。

translations.literal: Cong, style name Ziyi, was orphaned young and poor; with his elder brother Neng he together hid in the mountains of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cong, whose style name was Ziyi, lost his father early and grew up in poverty; he and his elder brother Neng withdrew together to live in the mountains near Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 會歲饑，拾橡實以飯，講學不廢。

translations.literal: When a year of famine came, they gathered acorns for food but did not cease their lectures and study.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year they subsisted on gathered acorns yet never interrupted their studies.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 從山南嚴震府為推官，以母喪免。

translations.literal: Cong served in the staff of Yan Zhen of Shannan as investigating officer and was dismissed on account of his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Cong served as investigating officer on Yan Zhen's staff in Shannan and left office when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 兄弟廬墓，手藝松柏。

translations.literal: The brothers built huts by the tomb and with their own hands planted pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers built mourning huts by the grave and planted pines and cypresses with their own hands.

sentences.zh: 喪闋，不應辟命。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, he did not respond to summons.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, he declined all summons to office.

sentences.zh: 久之，韋皋引為西山運務使。

translations.literal: After a long while, Wei Gao brought him in as transport commissioner of Xishan.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Wei Gao appointed him transport commissioner for the western hills.

sentences.zh: 奏遷判官，攝守邛州。

translations.literal: He was memorialized for promotion to staff judge and acted as defender of Qiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted on memorial to staff judge and served as acting prefect of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 前刺史有以盜繫獄，辭已具。

translations.literal: The former prefect had been imprisoned on a charge of theft; the confession was already complete.
translations.idiomatic: The previous prefect had been imprisoned for theft, and the case against him was already complete.

sentences.zh: 從疑其冤，縱不治，俄得真盜。

translations.literal: Cong suspected the man was wronged; he released him and did not prosecute, and soon the real thief was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Cong suspected a miscarriage of justice, released the man without proceeding, and soon captured the real thief.

sentences.zh: 皋卒，劉辟反，欲並東川。

translations.literal: When Gao died, Liu Pi rebelled and wished to annex Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao died, Liu Pi rebelled and sought to annex Dongchuan as well.

sentences.zh: 從以書諭止辟，辟怒，從乃募兵嬰城守。

translations.literal: Cong sent a letter admonishing Pi to stop; Pi was angry, and Cong then recruited troops and closed the city to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Cong wrote urging Pi to desist; when Pi grew enraged, Cong raised troops and held the city under siege.

sentences.zh: 辟方悉兵拒高崇文，戰而敗，從完州自如。

translations.literal: Pi had just deployed all his troops to resist Gao Chongwen; defeated in battle, Cong preserved the prefecture intact as before.
translations.idiomatic: Pi had massed his forces against Gao Chongwen, but after defeat Cong kept the prefecture intact as before.

sentences.zh: 盧坦表宣州副使。

translations.literal: Lu Tan memorialized him as vice-commissioner of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tan recommended him as vice-commissioner of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為殿中侍御史，遷吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Attendant Censor of the Palace and was promoted to Vice-Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as palace attendant censor and was promoted to vice-director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 異時，史給選者成牒，以先後丐賕，從一限出之，後遂為法。

translations.literal: In former times, clerks who issued selections would complete registers and beg bribes according to priority; Cong issued them within a single deadline, and afterward this became the rule.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, clerks who handled appointments would complete the registers and solicit bribes according to order of priority; Cong required all selections to be issued within one deadline, and this thereafter became standard practice.

sentences.zh: 裴度為御史中丞，奏以右司郎中知雜事。

translations.literal: When Pei Du was Censor-in-Chief, he memorialized that Cong, as Right Bureau Director, should manage miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du served as censor-in-chief, he had Cong, as right bureau director, manage the bureau's miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 度已相，代為中丞。

translations.literal: When Du had already become chief minister, Cong replaced him as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After Du became chief minister, Cong succeeded him as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 所彈治，不屈權幸。

translations.literal: In cases he impeached and punished, he did not yield to the powerful and favored.
translations.idiomatic: In his impeachments he never yielded to the powerful or the favored.

sentences.zh: 事系台閣而付仗內者，必請還有司。

translations.literal: Matters that belonged to the censorate but were handed to the inner palace guard always had to be requested back to the proper offices.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever cases under the censorate's jurisdiction were transferred to the inner palace guard, he insisted they be returned to the proper offices.

sentences.zh: 薦引御史，務取質重廉退者。

translations.literal: In recommending and bringing forward censors, he strove to select those of solid character, weight, and retiring integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In recommending censors he sought men of solid character, dignity, and retiring integrity.

sentences.zh: 李翛以寵得京兆尹，為莊憲太后山陵橋道使，務以減末徭費為功，至不治道輴車留渭橋，久不得進。

translations.literal: Li Xiao, through favor, became Metropolitan Magistrate of Jingzhao and served as commissioner for bridges and roads of Empress Dowager Zhuangxian's mausoleum, striving to make reducing minor corvée expenses his achievement, to the point that he did not repair the road and the funeral carriage remained at Weiqiao, long unable to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiao, favored at court, became metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao and commissioner for the mausoleum roads of Empress Dowager Zhuangxian; he made a show of cutting minor corvée costs, so that he neglected the road and the funeral carriage was stranded at Weiqiao for a long time.

sentences.zh: 從三劾之，無少貸。

translations.literal: Cong impeached him three times without the least leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Cong impeached him three times without the slightest leniency.

sentences.zh: 俄授陝虢觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Observation Commissioner of Shan-Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed observation commissioner of Shan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice-Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice-director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 王承宗請割德、棣而遣子入侍也，憲宗選堪使者，以命從。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong requested to cede De and Di and send his son to attend at court; Xianzong selected a capable envoy and entrusted Cong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chengzong offered to surrender De and Di prefectures and send his son to court as hostage, Xianzong chose a capable envoy and appointed Cong.

sentences.zh: 議者謂承宗狠譎，非單使可屈。

translations.literal: Discussants said Chengzong was fierce and crafty and could not be bent by a lone envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Chengzong was fierce and treacherous and could not be swayed by a lone envoy.

sentences.zh: 次魏，田弘正請以五百騎從，辭之，惟童騎十數，疾趨鎮。

translations.literal: Stopping at Wei, Tian Hongzheng requested to follow with five hundred horsemen; Cong declined, taking only a dozen or so mounted youths and hurrying to the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: At Wei, Tian Hongzheng offered five hundred horsemen as escort, but Cong declined and rode on with only a dozen youths, pressing swiftly to the garrison.

sentences.zh: 集軍士球場宣詔，為陳逆順大節禍福之效，音辭暢厲，士感動，承宗自失，貌愈恭，至泣下，即按二州戶口、符印上之。

translations.literal: He assembled the troops on the ball ground and proclaimed the edict, setting forth the great principle of loyalty and rebellion and the effect of fortune and misfortune; his voice and words were fluent and stern. The soldiers were moved; Chengzong lost himself, his bearing grew more respectful, even to weeping, and he immediately submitted the household registers and seals of the two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the troops on the drill ground, read the edict, and expounded the great principles of loyalty and rebellion and the consequences of fortune and ruin; his voice rang clear and forceful. The soldiers were moved; Chengzong was thrown off balance, grew ever more deferential, even to tears, and at once submitted the household registers and seals of the two prefectures.

sentences.zh: 還為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: On his return he became Military Commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 帝欲遂相，監軍使揣知，為用事者求金，從不肯答，用是不得相。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make him chief minister at once; the army supervisor divined this and, on behalf of those in power, sought gold. Cong would not answer, and for this reason he did not become chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to appoint him chief minister, but the army supervisor guessed this and, acting for those in power, demanded a bribe; Cong refused, and for that reason never received the post.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，繇尚書左丞領鄜坊節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, he went from Left Vice-Director of the Department of State Affairs to head the Bian-Fang command.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Changqing era he moved from left vice-director of the Department of State Affairs to military commissioner of Bian and Fang.

sentences.zh: 屬部多神策屯軍，數亂法驕橫，吏不能制，從一繩以法，下皆重足畏之。

translations.literal: In his jurisdiction were many encamped troops of the Shence Army, who repeatedly violated the law in arrogant violence and whom officials could not control; Cong applied the law uniformly, and all below walked as if on overlapping feet in fear of him.
translations.idiomatic: His jurisdiction held many Shence encampments whose troops repeatedly broke the law in arrogant defiance; officials could not control them, but Cong applied the law without exception until all below trembled before him.

sentences.zh: 党項互市羊馬，類先遺帥守，從獨不取，而厚慰待之，羌不敢盜境。

translations.literal: When the Tangut tribes traded sheep and horses at the border markets, they usually first presented gifts to the commander and defender; Cong alone did not take them, yet treated them generously and kindly, and the Qiang did not dare raid the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Tangut tribes came to trade sheep and horses, commanders usually accepted gifts in advance; Cong alone refused them yet treated the traders generously, and the Qiang did not dare raid his border.

sentences.zh: 寶曆初，為東都留守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoli, he became Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Baoli era he became defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 故事，留司官入宮城門列晨衙見留守。

translations.literal: By precedent, officials of the capital staff who entered the palace-city gate lined up for morning court to see the defender.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, capital staff who entered the palace-city gate would line up for morning audience with the defender.

sentences.zh: 吏誕傲，久廢，至是復行。

translations.literal: Officials had grown arrogant and it had long been abandoned; at this time it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Officials had grown arrogant and the custom had long lapsed; Cong restored it.

sentences.zh: 召拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 宰相李宗閔以從裴度、李德裕所善，內不喜。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Zongmin, because Cong was favored by Pei Du and Li Deyu, inwardly disliked him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Li Zongmin disliked Cong inwardly because he was close to Pei Du and Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 從求致仕，除太子賓客，分司東都，告滿百日去。

translations.literal: Cong requested retirement; he was made Guest of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital, and after reporting his full hundred days he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Cong asked to retire and was made guest of the heir apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital; after completing the required hundred-day notice he left office.

sentences.zh: 於是眾嘩語不平，宗閔懼，復授檢校尚書左僕射、淮南節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the crowd clamored in discontent; Zongmin was afraid and again appointed him Acting Left Vice-Director of the Department of State Affairs, Vice Commissioner of the Huainan command, with control of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The public outcry was so loud that Zongmin grew alarmed and reappointed him acting left vice-director of the Department of State Affairs and vice commissioner of Huainan with control of the circuit.

sentences.zh: 揚州凡交易貲產、奴婢有貫率錢，畜羊有口算，又貿曲牟其贏，以佐用度，從皆蠲除之。

translations.literal: At Yangzhou, for every transaction of property and slaves there was a per-string levy, for kept sheep there was a per-head tax, and moreover they traded in yeast to mulct the profits to supplement expenses; Cong abolished them all.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangzhou every transaction in property or slaves carried a per-string levy, every sheep a head tax, and officials also profited on yeast sales to pad expenses; Cong abolished all of these.

sentences.zh: 官吏俸帛常加倍以給，獨節度使則否，從皆與之同。

translations.literal: Officials' salary silks were usually given at double the rate, but the military commissioner alone was not; Cong gave him the same as the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' salary silks were usually paid at double rate, but the military commissioner alone was excluded; Cong extended the double payment to himself as well.

sentences.zh: 大和六年卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dahe he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Dahe, at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 下有刲股肉以祭者。

translations.literal: Among those below were some who cut flesh from their thighs to offer in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his subordinates cut flesh from their thighs as a mourning sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 贈司空，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of works, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 從為人嚴偉，立朝棱棱有風望，不喜交權利，忠厚而讓。

translations.literal: Cong as a man was stern and imposing; in court he stood angular with commanding reputation, disliking association with power and profit, loyal and thick yet yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was stern and imposing in bearing; in court he stood out with commanding dignity, shunned dealings in power and profit, and was loyal, generous, and self-effacing.

sentences.zh: 階品當立門戟，終不請。

translations.literal: His rank entitled him to set up gate halberds, yet he never requested them.
translations.idiomatic: His rank entitled him to ceremonial gate halberds, yet he never requested them.

sentences.zh: 位方鎮，內無聲妓娛玩。

translations.literal: Though he held a frontier command, within he had no singing girls or diversions.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held a frontier command, he kept no singers or entertainers in his household.

sentences.zh: 士大夫賢之。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials deemed him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Men of letters esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 曾孫 能能，字子才。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Neng — Neng, style name Zicai.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson was Neng, whose style name was Zicai.

sentences.zh: 硃泚之亂，渾瑊以朔方軍戰武功，引佐幕府。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Zhu Ci, Hun Jian fought at Wugong with the Shuofang army and brought Neng in to assist the staff.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's rebellion, Hun Jian fought at Wugong with the Shuofang army and brought Neng onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 進累侍御史。

translations.literal: He advanced through repeated appointments as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments as attending censor.

sentences.zh: 河東鄭儋表為判官。

translations.literal: Zheng Dan of Hedong memorialized him as staff judge.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Dan of Hedong recommended him as staff judge.

sentences.zh: 累遷黔中觀察使，以讒坐貶。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Observation Commissioner of Qianzhong and, on account of slander, was demoted for his offense.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to observation commissioner of Qianzhong but was demoted after falling victim to slander.

sentences.zh: 從為中丞，奏以自代。

translations.literal: When Cong was Censor-in-Chief, he memorialized that Neng should replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong became censor-in-chief, he memorialized that Neng should succeed him.

sentences.zh: 繇將作監授嶺南節度使，與從皆秉節居鎮，世傳為榮。

translations.literal: He went from Director of Palace Construction to Military Commissioner of Lingnan; he and Cong both held the tally and dwelt in command, transmitted through generations as glory.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced from director of palace construction to military commissioner of Lingnan; he and Cong both held frontier commands at the same time, a distinction their family long prized.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十八，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-eight, and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-eight and was posthumously made minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 從子慎由、安潛。

translations.literal: Nephews of Cong: Shenyou and An Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's nephews were Shenyou and An Qian.

sentences.zh: 能子彥曾。

translations.literal: Neng's son Yanzeng.
translations.idiomatic: Neng's son was Yanzeng.

sentences.zh: 能從子 慎由慎由，字敬止。

translations.literal: Neng's nephew Cong's nephew Shenyou — Shenyou, style name Jingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Neng's nephew Shenyou, whose style name was Jingzhi.

sentences.zh: 聰警強記，資端厚，有父風采。

translations.literal: He was clever and alert with a strong memory, endowed with upright substance and thickness, and had his father's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted with a formidable memory, upright and steady in character, and bore his father's dignity.

sentences.zh: 繇進士第擢賢良方正異等。

translations.literal: From the jinshi degree he was elevated to extraordinary grade in the Worthy and Upright examination.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he was elevated to the highest grade in the Worthy and Upright examination.

sentences.zh: 鄭滑高銖辟府判官。

translations.literal: Gao Chu of Zheng-Hua recruited him as staff judge.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chu of Zheng-Hua recruited him as a staff judge.

sentences.zh: 入為右拾遺，進翰林學士。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Right Reminder and advanced to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as right reminder and was promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 授湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Observation Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed observation commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 召還，由刑部侍郎領浙西。

translations.literal: He was recalled; from Vice-Director of the Ministry of Justice he headed Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and, as vice-director of the Ministry of Justice, took charge of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 入遷戶部侍郎，判戶部。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was promoted to Vice-Director of the Ministry of Revenue, with control of that ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital, was promoted to vice-director of the Ministry of Revenue, and assumed control of the ministry.

sentences.zh: 始，慎由苦目疾，不得視，醫為治刮，適愈而召。

translations.literal: At first Shenyou suffered from eye disease and could not see; a physician treated him by scraping, and just as he recovered he was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shenyou had suffered a painful eye ailment that left him blind; a physician scraped his eyes to treat him, and he had just recovered when the summons came.

sentences.zh: 俄進工部尚書、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Minister of Works and Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to minister of works and associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 與蕭鄴有隙，鄴輔政，引劉瑑，而出慎由為東川節度使。

translations.literal: He had a rift with Xiao Ye; when Ye assisted in government, he brought in Liu Zhuan and sent Shenyou out as Military Commissioner of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had fallen out with Xiao Ye; when Ye took power he brought in Liu Zhuan and transferred Shenyou to military commissioner of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 初，宣宗餌長年藥，病渴且中躁，而國嗣未立。

translations.literal: At first Xuānzong took longevity elixirs, suffered thirst and inner agitation, and the heir to the state had not yet been established.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xuānzong had taken longevity elixirs, which left him thirsty and irritable, while the succession remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 帝對宰相欲肆赦，患無其端。

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief ministers he wished to proclaim a general amnesty but worried there was no occasion for it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his chief ministers he wished to proclaim a general amnesty but lacked a suitable pretext.

sentences.zh: 慎由曰：「太子，天下本。

translations.literal: Shenyou said: "The crown prince is the root of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyou said: "The crown prince is the foundation of the realm.

sentences.zh: 若立之，赦為有名。」

translations.literal: If he is established, the amnesty will have a name.
translations.idiomatic: If you establish him, the amnesty will have a proper justification.

sentences.zh: 帝惡之，不答。

translations.literal: The emperor hated this and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense and made no reply.

sentences.zh: 鄴等乘是譖去之，時大中十二年也。

translations.literal: Ye and others seized on this to slander him and remove him; it was the twelfth year of Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ye and his allies used the remark to slander him out of office; this was in the twelfth year of Dazhong.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，徙華州刺史，改河中節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he was transferred to Prefect of Huazhou and changed to Military Commissioner of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xiantong era he was transferred to prefect of Huazhou and then made military commissioner of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 以吏部尚書請老，授太子太保，分司東都。

translations.literal: As Minister of Personnel he requested retirement on account of age and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of personnel he asked to retire and was made grand guardian of the heir apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works, with posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of works, with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 子胤，別傳。

translations.literal: His son Yin has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 能從子 安潛安潛，字進之。

translations.literal: Neng's nephew Cong's nephew An Qian — An Qian, style name Jinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Neng's nephew An Qian, whose style name was Jinzhi.

sentences.zh: 進士擢第。

translations.literal: He was selected in the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，曆江西觀察、忠武節度使。

translations.literal: During Xiantong he successively served as Observation Commissioner of Jiangxi and Military Commissioner of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantong era he served successively as observation commissioner of Jiangxi and military commissioner of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 乾符初，王仙芝寇河南，安潛募人增陴繕械，不以力費仰朝廷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu, Wang Xianzhi raided Henan; An Qian recruited men, heightened walls, and repaired weapons without relying on the court for labor expenses.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qianfu era, when Wang Xianzhi raided Henan, An Qian raised troops, strengthened the walls, and repaired arms without asking the court to bear the cost.

sentences.zh: 首請會兵討捕，號令精明，賊畏之，不犯陳許境。

translations.literal: He was the first to request united troops for pursuit and capture; his orders were sharp and clear, the bandits feared him, and they did not invade the Chen-Xu region.
translations.idiomatic: He was the first to call for combined forces to hunt the rebels; his commands were precise, the bandits feared him, and they did not enter the Chen-Xu circuit.

sentences.zh: 使大將張自勉將兵七千援宋州。

translations.literal: He sent his great general Zhang Zimian to lead seven thousand troops to relieve Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his chief general Zhang Zimian with seven thousand men to relieve Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 時宋威屯曹州，而官軍數卻，賊圍宋益急。

translations.literal: At the time Song Wei was encamped at Caozhou, but government troops had repeatedly retreated and the rebels pressed the siege of Song ever tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wei was then encamped at Caozhou, but government forces had suffered repeated setbacks and the rebels tightened their siege of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 自勉收南月城，斬賊二千級，仙芝夜解去。

translations.literal: Zimian recovered Nanyue City and beheaded two thousand bandits; Xianzhi lifted the siege by night and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zimian recaptured Nanyue City and killed two thousand rebels; Xianzhi raised the siege overnight and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 宰相鄭畋建言：「請以陳許兵三千隸宋威。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zheng Tian proposed: "Please assign three thousand Chen-Xu troops to Song Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zheng Tian proposed: "Let three thousand Chen-Xu troops be placed under Song Wei.

sentences.zh: 而威忌自勉，乞盡得安潛軍，使自勉隸麾下。

translations.literal: But Wei resented Zimian and begged to obtain all of An Qian's army and have Zimian placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: But Wei resented Zimian and asked to take all of An Qian's troops and place Zimian under his own command.

sentences.zh: 畋謂威有疑忿，必殺自勉，奏言：「今以兵悉畀威，是自勉以功受辱。

translations.literal: Tian said Wei harbored suspicion and resentment and would surely kill Zimian; he memorialized: "Now to give all the troops to Wei is to let Zimian be shamed despite his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tian said Wei was jealous and would surely kill Zimian; he memorialized: "To hand all these troops to Wei would humiliate Zimian despite his achievements.

sentences.zh: 安潛抗賊有功，乃取銳兵付威，後有緩急，何以戰？

translations.literal: An Qian resisted the bandits with merit; yet you take his crack troops and give them to Wei—when urgency comes later, how will he fight?
translations.idiomatic: An Qian has fought the rebels with distinction; if you strip him of his best troops for Wei, how will he meet the next emergency?

sentences.zh: 是勞不蒙賞，無以示天下。」

translations.literal: This is labor unrewarded, with no way to show the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Merit would go unrewarded, and the court would lose credibility throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 詔止以四千付威，餘還自勉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that only four thousand be given to Wei; the rest returned to Zimian.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered only four thousand men transferred to Wei; the rest returned to Zimian.

sentences.zh: 俄代高駢領西川節度。

translations.literal: Soon he replaced Gao Pian in heading the Xichuan command.
translations.idiomatic: He soon replaced Gao Pian as military commissioner of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 吏倚駢為奸利者，安潛皆誅之，數更除繆政，於是盜賊衰，蜀民以安。

translations.literal: Officials who relied on Pian for illicit profit were all executed by An Qian; he repeatedly revised and abolished corrupt policies, and thereafter bandits declined and the people of Shu were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: He executed officials who had profited through Pian's patronage, repealed corrupt policies one after another, and banditry waned until the people of Shu lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 宰相盧攜素厚駢，乃誣以罪，罷為太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Lu Xie had long been close to Pian and therefore slandered An Qian with crimes, demoting him to Guest of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Lu Xie, who had long favored Pian, trumped up charges against An Qian and demoted him to guest of the heir apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 僖宗避賊劍南，召為太子少師。

translations.literal: When Xizong fled the bandits to Jiannan, An Qian was summoned as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong fled the rebels to Jiannan, An Qian was summoned as junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 王鐸任都統，表以自副。

translations.literal: When Wang Duo served as supreme commander, he memorialized that An Qian should serve as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Duo became supreme commander, he recommended An Qian as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 鐸解兵，安潛復為少師、東都留守。

translations.literal: When Duo relinquished command, An Qian again became Junior Tutor and Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Duo laid down his command, An Qian again became junior tutor and defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 青州王敬武卒，詔拜平盧節度使，檢校太師兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Wang Jingwu of Qingzhou died, an edict appointed An Qian Military Commissioner of Pinglu, with acting title Grand Preceptor and concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingwu of Qingzhou died, the court appointed An Qian military commissioner of Pinglu with the acting titles of grand preceptor and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 會敬武子師範專地，不得入而還。

translations.literal: It happened that Jingwu's son Shifan held the territory exclusively; An Qian could not enter and returned.
translations.idiomatic: But Jingwu's son Shifan controlled the territory and barred his entry, so he turned back.

sentences.zh: 後遷太子太傅。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太師，諡貞孝。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, with posthumous title Zhenxiao.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made grand preceptor of the heir apparent, with the posthumous name Zhenxiao.

sentences.zh: 安潛于吏事尤長，雖位將相，閱具獄，未嘗不身聽之。

translations.literal: An Qian was especially skilled in administrative affairs; though he reached the rank of general or minister, when reviewing completed cases he never failed to hear them in person.
translations.idiomatic: An Qian excelled above all in administrative affairs; even at ministerial rank he personally heard every completed case brought before him.

sentences.zh: 能子 彥曾彥曾，咸通初，繇太僕卿為徐州觀察使。

translations.literal: Neng's son Yanzeng — Yanzeng, at the beginning of Xiantong, went from Director of the Imperial Stud to Observation Commissioner of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Neng's son Yanzeng, at the start of the Xiantong era, moved from director of the imperial stud to observation commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 曉律令，然卞急，為政剛猛。

translations.literal: He understood statutes and ordinances, yet was abrupt and impatient, governing with stern severity.
translations.idiomatic: He knew the law well but was brusque and impatient, governing with harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 徐軍素驕，而彥曾長於撫民，短治軍，士多怨之。

translations.literal: The Xuzhou army had long been arrogant; Yanzeng was skilled at comforting the people but weak in governing troops, and the soldiers resented him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuzhou garrison had long been unruly; Yanzeng was adept at winning over civilians but poor at managing troops, and the men resented him.

sentences.zh: 初，蠻寇五管，陷交趾，詔節度使孟球募兵三千往屯，以八百人戍桂林。

translations.literal: At first the barbarians raided the Five Circuits, captured Jiaozhi, and an edict ordered Military Commissioner Meng Qiu to recruit three thousand troops to encamp there, with eight hundred men garrisoning Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when southern tribes raided the Five Circuits and captured Jiaozhi, the court ordered Military Commissioner Meng Qiu to raise three thousand men for the campaign and garrison eight hundred at Guilin.

sentences.zh: 舊制，三年一更。

translations.literal: By old regulation, they were replaced every three years.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation they were rotated every three years.

sentences.zh: 至期請代，而彥曾親吏尹戡、徐行儉貪不恤士，乃議稟賜乏，請無發兵，復留屯一年。

translations.literal: When the term came they requested relief, but Yanzeng's close clerks Yin Kan and Xu Xingjian were greedy and did not care for the troops; they therefore proposed that stipends and gifts were lacking, begged that no relief troops be sent, and kept the garrison another year.
translations.idiomatic: When their term ended they asked to be relieved, but Yanzeng's trusted clerks Yin Kan and Xu Xingjian, greedy and indifferent to the soldiers' welfare, claimed funds for rations and rewards were short, refused to send replacements, and kept the garrison another year.

sentences.zh: 戍者怒，殺都將王仲甫，脅糧料判官龐勳為將，取庫兵，剽湘、衡，虜丁壯，合眾千餘北還，自浙西趨淮南，達泗口。

translations.literal: The garrison troops were enraged; they killed the commander Wang Zhongfu, forced the grain-supply judge Pang Xun to be their general, seized arsenal weapons, plundered Xiang and Heng, seized able-bodied men, gathered more than a thousand and returned north, from Zhexi hastened toward Huainan, and reached Sikou.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison rose in fury, killed Commander Wang Zhongfu, and forced grain-supply judge Pang Xun to lead them; they seized arsenal weapons, raided Xiang and Heng, took captives, and with more than a thousand men marched north from Zhexi through Huainan to Sikou.

sentences.zh: 所過先遣俳兒弄木偶，伺人情，以防邀遏。

translations.literal: Where they passed they first sent jesters to perform with puppets, spy on popular sentiment, and guard against interception.
translations.idiomatic: Along the route they sent jesters ahead with puppet shows to gauge local sentiment and avoid interception.

sentences.zh: 彥曾命牙將田厚簡慰勞，而用都虞候元密伏甲任山館擊賊。

translations.literal: Yanzeng ordered his牙-general Tian Houjian to offer comfort and rewards, but used the chief commandant Yuan Mi to set an ambush with armor at Renshan Lodge to strike the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzeng sent his adjutant Tian Houjian with words of comfort while setting Chief Commandant Yuan Mi in ambush at Renshan Lodge to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 勳遣吏紿言士思歸，不敢遏，請至府解甲自歸，彥曾斬其吏。

translations.literal: Xun sent an official to deceive them, saying the troops wished to return home and dared not obstruct them, and asking to come to the prefectural seat to lay down arms and surrender themselves; Yanzeng beheaded the official.
translations.idiomatic: Xun sent an envoy falsely claiming his men only wanted to go home and asking to surrender at the prefectural seat; Yanzeng had the envoy beheaded.

sentences.zh: 勳陷宿州，發廥錢募兵，亡命者從亂如歸，船千艘，與騎夾岸，噪而進。

translations.literal: Xun seized Suzhou, issued treasury funds to recruit troops, and fugitives joined the rebellion as if returning home; a thousand boats and cavalry lined both banks, shouting as they advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Xun captured Suzhou, spent treasury funds to recruit troops, and fugitives flocked to him; a thousand boats and horsemen lined both banks, advancing with a clamor.

sentences.zh: 彥曾料丁男乘城。

translations.literal: Yanzeng conscripted adult males to man the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzeng drafted every able-bodied man onto the walls.

sentences.zh: 或勸率眾奔兗州，彥曾曰：「我，方帥也，奉命守此，惟有死爾。」

translations.literal: Some urged him to lead the crowd and flee to Yanzhou; Yanzeng said: "I am a frontier commander, ordered to defend this place—there is only death.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to abandon the city and flee to Yanzhou; Yanzeng replied: "I am a frontier commander charged to hold this post. I can only die here.

sentences.zh: 斬議者一人號於眾。

translations.literal: He beheaded one who had argued thus and displayed him before the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded one adviser and displayed the head before the troops.

sentences.zh: 俄而勳傅城，城中大霧如墮。

translations.literal: Soon Xun pressed the city; within the walls a great fog fell as if from the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xun invested the city, and a dense fog settled over it as if the sky had fallen.

sentences.zh: 彥曾悉誅賊家屬，勳眾四面超墉入，囚彥曾大彭館。

translations.literal: Yanzeng executed all the bandits' families; Xun's host scaled the walls on four sides and entered, imprisoning Yanzeng in the Great Peng Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzeng had executed the rebels' families; Xun's men scaled the walls on every side, seized the city, and imprisoned Yanzeng in the Great Peng Lodge.

sentences.zh: 有曹君長者說勳曰：「貴者不並處，今朝廷未以留後命公，蓋觀察使存爾。」

translations.literal: A certain Cao Junzhang advised Xun: "The noble do not dwell together; now the court has not given you the post of acting commissioner—surely it is because the observation commissioner still lives.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Cao Junzhang told Xun: "Two masters cannot share one seat. The court has not named you acting commissioner because the observation commissioner is still alive.

sentences.zh: 勳乃殺彥曾於寢，自監軍使逮官屬皆死。

translations.literal: Xun then killed Yanzeng in his bedchamber; from the army supervisor down, all officials died.
translations.idiomatic: Xun then killed Yanzeng in his quarters, and every official from the army supervisor down was put to death.

sentences.zh: 始，彥曾治第鄭州，引水灌沼，水十步忽化為血。

translations.literal: At first, when Yanzeng built a mansion in Zhengzhou and led water to fill a pond, within ten paces the water suddenly turned to blood.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while building a mansion in Zhengzhou, he had water led into a pond; within ten paces the water suddenly turned to blood.

sentences.zh: 署張佛筵，液蜜為人，一昔鼠齧皆斷首。

translations.literal: He set out a spread for the Buddha with figures made of honey syrup; in one night rats gnawed them all headless.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared a Buddhist offering with figures molded from honey; overnight rats gnawed off every head.

sentences.zh: 徐有子亭，下瀦水為沱，彥曾導清河灌之，鐫石龍首注溜，蔽以屋。

translations.literal: Xuzhou had the Zi Pavilion; below it water was dammed to form a pool. Yanzeng channeled the Qing River to irrigate it, carved a stone dragon head for the outflow, and roofed it with a building.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou had the Zi Pavilion with a dammed pool beneath it; Yanzeng diverted the Qing River to fill it, carved a stone dragon head for the outlet, and roofed it over.

sentences.zh: 徐人謂屋覆龍，于文為「龐」；

translations.literal: The people of Xu said a building covering a dragon, in written form, is "Pang";
translations.idiomatic: Locals said a roof covering a dragon (long) formed the character for "Pang";

sentences.zh: 清河，崔望也，為吞噬雲。

translations.literal: the Qing River is the surname Cui's hope, signifying devouring and swallowing.
translations.idiomatic: and the Qing River, homophone for the Cui clan's surname, foretold devouring and ruin.

sentences.zh: 贈刑部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，錄其子祐之為滎陽尉。

translations.literal: During Qianfu his son Youzhi was entered on the rolls as magistrate of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianfu era his son Youzhi was appointed magistrate of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 徐吏有路審中者，彥曾知其能，頗任之。

translations.literal: Among Xuzhou officials there was Lu Shenzhong; Yanzeng knew his ability and greatly entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Among Yanzeng's staff was Lu Shenzhong, whom he recognized as capable and entrusted with important duties.

sentences.zh: 既遇害，賂守卒，斂藏其屍。

translations.literal: After Yanzeng was killed, Shenzhong bribed the guards, gathered and hid his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanzeng was killed, Shenzhong bribed the guards and secretly recovered his body.

sentences.zh: 張玄稔攻徐州；

translations.literal: Zhang Xuanchen attacked Xuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xuanchen attacked Xuzhou,

sentences.zh: 審中率死士應官軍，開南白門，官兵入，因得破勳。

translations.literal: Shenzhong led dare-to-die troops to join the government army, opened the south White Gate, government troops entered, and thus they were able to defeat Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhong led a suicide squad to aid the government forces, opened the south White Gate, let the troops in, and helped break Xun's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 後位嵐州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he held the post of Prefect of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later became prefect of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄭畋謂審中節貫神明，請擢為右羽林將軍，詔可。

translations.literal: Zheng Tian said Shenzhong's integrity penetrated the divine; he requested his promotion to General of the Right Yulin Guard, and an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tian declared Shenzhong's integrity almost supernatural and recommended him as general of the Right Yulin Guard; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 有許鐸者，罷武城令，客于徐，勳脅以官，不從。

translations.literal: There was a Xu Duo who, dismissed as magistrate of Wucheng, sojourned in Xu; Xun coerced him with office, but he would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: A former magistrate of Wucheng named Xu Duo was staying in Xuzhou when Xun tried to force an office on him; he refused.

sentences.zh: 彥曾官屬被囚，鐸潛饋資糧，及死，為收瘞，匿免其子弟，賊平，乃皆歸其喪。

translations.literal: When Yanzeng's staff were imprisoned, Duo secretly supplied provisions; when Yanzeng died, he gathered and buried him, hid and spared his sons and younger brothers, and after the bandits were pacified returned all their coffins.
translations.idiomatic: While Yanzeng's staff lay imprisoned, Duo secretly supplied them; after Yanzeng's death he buried the body, sheltered his sons and brothers, and when the rebellion ended restored their remains to the family.

sentences.zh: 詔拜石首令，賜銀緋。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him magistrate of Shishou and bestowed silver seals and scarlet robes.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed him magistrate of Shishou and awarded him silver seals and scarlet robes.

sentences.zh: 僚官焦璐、溫廷皓、李棁、崔蘊、柳秦、盧崇嗣、韋廷範贈官有差，錄其子官之。

translations.literal: Staff officials Jiao Lu, Wen Tinghao, Li Zhi, Cui Yun, Liu Qin, Lu Chongsi, and Wei Tingfan received posthumous offices in varying degrees, and their sons were entered on the rolls for office.
translations.idiomatic: Staff members Jiao Lu, Wen Tinghao, Li Zhi, Cui Yun, Liu Qin, Lu Chongsi, and Wei Tingfan received posthumous offices in varying ranks, and their sons were granted official appointments.

sentences.zh: 徐彥伯徐彥伯，兗州瑕丘人，名洪，以字顯。

translations.literal: Xu Yanbo — Xu Yanbo, a man of Xiaqiu in Yanzhou; his name was Hong, but he was known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanbo was a native of Xiaqiu in Yanzhou; his personal name was Hong, but he was known by his style name.

sentences.zh: 七歲能為文。

translations.literal: At seven he could compose writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seven he could already write essays.

sentences.zh: 結廬太行山下。

translations.literal: He built a hut beneath Mount Taihang.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hut at the foot of Mount Taihang.

sentences.zh: 薛元超安撫河北，表其賢，對策高第。

translations.literal: When Xue Yuanchao pacified Hebei, he memorialized Yanbo's worth; in the policy examination he ranked at the top.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Yuanchao pacified Hebei he recommended Yanbo's talent, and Yanbo took top honors in the policy examination.

sentences.zh: 調永壽尉、蒲州司兵參軍。

translations.literal: He was assigned as magistrate of Yongshou and military staff officer of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yongshou and military staff officer in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 時司戶韋皓善判，司士李亙工書，而彥伯屬辭，時稱「河東三絕」。

translations.literal: At the time Revenue Registrar Wei Hao was skilled in judgments, Records Clerk Li Gen excelled at calligraphy, and Yanbo composed literary pieces; they were called at the time "the Three Unsurpassed of Hedong."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hao, revenue registrar, excelled at legal judgments; Li Gen, records clerk, at calligraphy; and Yanbo at literary composition—they were known as the "Three Unsurpassed of Hedong."

sentences.zh: 遷職方員外郎，奉迎中宗房州，進給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice-Director of the Bureau of Appointments, welcomed Zhongzong at Fangzhou, and advanced to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice-director of the Bureau of Appointments, welcomed Zhongzong at Fangzhou, and advanced to drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 武后撰《三教珠英》，取文辭士，皆天下選，而彥伯、李嶠居首。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu compiled the Pearls of the Three Teachings, she selected men of literary talent from throughout the realm; Yanbo and Li Jiao stood at the head.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu compiled the 《Pearls of the Three Teachings》, she chose literary men from across the empire; Yanbo and Li Jiao ranked first.

sentences.zh: 遷宗正卿，出為齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Imperial Clan and sent out as Prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the imperial clan and then sent out as prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 帝復位，改太常少卿。

translations.literal: When the emperor regained the throne, Yanbo was changed to Vice-Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was restored to the throne, Yanbo was made vice-director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 以脩《武后實錄》勞，封高平縣子。

translations.literal: For labor in compiling the Veritable Records of Empress Wu, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: For compiling the 《Veritable Records of Empress Wu》, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 為衛州刺史，政善狀，璽書嘉勞。

translations.literal: As Prefect of Weizhou his governance earned excellent reports, and an imperial letter praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Weizhou he earned excellent evaluations, and the emperor sent a letter of praise and reward.

sentences.zh: 移蒲州，以近畿，會郊祭，上《南郊賦》一篇，辭致黃縟。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Puzhou; because it was near the capital, when the suburban sacrifice occurred he submitted one piece, "Rhapsody on the Southern Suburb," with diction ornate and lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Puzhou near the capital, he submitted his "Rhapsody on the Southern Suburb" for the suburban sacrifice—its diction sumptuous and ornate.

sentences.zh: 擢脩文館學士、工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was elevated to Scholar of the Xiūwen Hall and Vice-Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to scholar of the Xiūwen Hall and vice-director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 曆太子賓客。

translations.literal: He successively served as Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as guest of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 以疾乞骸骨，許之。

translations.literal: On account of illness he begged to retire with his bones; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led him to request retirement, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 開元二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 彥伯事寡嫂謹，撫諸侄同己子。

translations.literal: Yanbo served his widowed sister-in-law with care and raised his nephews as his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo treated his widowed sister-in-law with scrupulous care and raised his nephews as if they were his own sons.

sentences.zh: 秉筆累朝，後來翕然慕仿。

translations.literal: He wielded the brush through successive reigns, and those who came after all at once admired and imitated him.
translations.idiomatic: He served as court writer through several reigns, and later generations emulated him wholesale.

sentences.zh: 晚為文稍強澀，然當時不及也。

translations.literal: In his later years his writing grew somewhat forceful and obdurate, yet at the time none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: His late style grew somewhat forceful and austere, yet in his day he still had no equal.

sentences.zh: 始，武后時，大獄興，王公卿士以語言為酷吏所引，死徙不可計。

translations.literal: At first, in the time of Empress Wu, great prisons arose; princes, dukes, and scholar-officials were implicated by their words through cruel officials, and those who died or were banished could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under Empress Wu, great political persecutions arose; princes, ministers, and officials were ensnared by their words through cruel investigators, and the dead and exiled were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 彥伯著《樞機論》以謂：「言者，德之柄，行之主，志之端，身之文也。

translations.literal: Yanbo wrote the Discourse on the Pivot and said: "Speech is the handle of virtue, the master of conduct, the tip of intent, and the ornament of the person.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo wrote the 《Discourse on the Pivot》, arguing: "Speech is the handle of virtue, the master of action, the outward edge of intent, and the ornament of the self.

sentences.zh: 君子之樞機，動則物應，得失之見也。

translations.literal: The pivot of the gentleman—when it moves, things respond; it is where gain and loss become visible.
translations.idiomatic: For the gentleman it is the pivot: when it moves, the world responds, and gain and loss become visible.

sentences.zh: 可以濟身，亦以覆身，否泰榮辱一系之。

translations.literal: It can save the person, and it can also overturn the person; adversity and ease, glory and disgrace all hang upon it.
translations.idiomatic: It can sustain a life or ruin one; fortune and misfortune, honor and shame all depend upon it.

sentences.zh: 能審思而應，精慮而動，擇其交以後談，則悔吝何由而生？

translations.literal: If one can deliberate carefully before responding, reflect finely before acting, and choose one's associations before speaking afterward, from what could regret and shame arise?
translations.idiomatic: If one thinks carefully before speaking, reflects deeply before acting, and chooses one's company before confiding, how could regret or shame arise?

sentences.zh: 怨惡何由而至？

translations.literal: From what could hatred and malice come?
translations.idiomatic: How could hatred and malice arise?

sentences.zh: 如此乃可以言也。」

translations.literal: Only thus may one speak."
translations.idiomatic: Only then is speech permissible."

sentences.zh: 以為戒世雲。

translations.literal: He offered this as a warning to the age.
translations.idiomatic: He intended this as a warning to his age.

sentences.zh: 蘇味道蘇味道，趙州欒城人。

translations.literal: Su Weidao — Su Weidao, a man of Luancheng in Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Weidao was a native of Luancheng in Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 九歲能屬辭，與裏人李嶠俱以文翰顯，時號「蘇李」。

translations.literal: At nine he could compose literary pieces; with his fellow townsman Li Jiao he both became famous for letters and were called at the time "Su and Li."
translations.idiomatic: At nine he could already compose literary pieces; he and his fellow townsman Li Jiao won fame for their writing and were known together as "Su and Li."

sentences.zh: 逮冠，州舉進士，中第。

translations.literal: When he reached cap age, the prefecture recommended him for the jinshi examination and he passed.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching adulthood he was recommended by the prefecture for the jinshi examination and passed.

sentences.zh: 累調咸陽尉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly assigned as magistrate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly posted as magistrate of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎裴行儉才之，會征突厥，引管書記。

translations.literal: Pei Xingjian, Vice-Director of the Ministry of Personnel, recognized his talent; when a campaign against the Turks was launched, he brought Weidao in to manage records.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian, vice-director of the Ministry of Personnel, recognized his talent and, during the campaign against the Turks, took him on as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 裴居道為左金吾衛將軍，倩味道作章，攬筆而具，閑徹清密，當時盛傳。

translations.literal: When Pei Judao was General of the Left Golden Crow Guard, he asked Weidao to compose a memorial; Weidao took up the brush and completed it at once, lucid and refined throughout, and it was widely circulated at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Judao served as general of the Left Golden Crow Guard, he asked Weidao to draft a memorial; Weidao took up the brush and finished it at once in language lucid and refined, and the piece was widely admired.

sentences.zh: 延載中，以鳳閣舍人檢校侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事，歲餘為真。

translations.literal: During Yanzai, as Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion he served as acting vice-director and Associate Chief Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace; after more than a year he received the full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanzai era he served as attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion with acting vice-director rank and as associate chief minister; after a year he received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 證聖元年，與張錫俱坐法系司刑獄。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengsheng, he and Zhang Xi together were implicated by the legal code and imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengsheng he and Zhang Xi were both imprisoned under the Ministry of Justice on legal charges.

sentences.zh: 錫雖下吏，氣象自如，味道獨席地飯蔬，為危惴可憐者。

translations.literal: Though Xi was sent down to the clerks, his bearing remained at ease; Weidao alone sat on the ground eating vegetables, a figure of fearful dread and pity.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xi remained composed even in custody, Weidao alone sat on the bare ground eating vegetables, a pitiable figure of constant dread.

sentences.zh: 武后聞，放錫嶺南，才降味道集州刺史。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu heard of this, she released Xi to Lingnan and only demoted Weidao to Prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu heard of this, she exiled Xi to Lingnan and merely demoted Weidao to prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 召為天官侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice-Director of the Bureau of the Heavens.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice-director of the Bureau of the Heavens.

sentences.zh: 聖曆初，復以鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenglì he again served as Vice-Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Third-Rank Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shenglì era he again became vice-director of the Phoenix Pavilion and third-rank associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 更葬其親，有詔州縣治喪事。

translations.literal: He reburied his parents, and an edict ordered the prefecture and county to manage the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When he reburied his parents, an edict ordered the local authorities to manage the funeral.

sentences.zh: 味道因役庸過程，遂侵毀鄉人墓田，蕭至忠劾之，貶坊州刺史。

translations.literal: Weidao, because corvée labor exceeded the schedule, encroached on and destroyed a fellow townsman's grave fields; Xiao Zhizhong impeached him and he was demoted to Prefect of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao's corvée work ran over schedule and he damaged a neighbor's grave land; Xiao Zhizhong impeached him and he was demoted to prefect of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Administrator of the Yizhou Grand Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief administrator of the Yizhou grand protectorate.

sentences.zh: 張易之敗，坐黨附，貶眉州刺史。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yizhi fell, Weidao was punished for partisan attachment and demoted to Prefect of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yizhi's fall he was punished for partisan association and demoted to prefect of Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 復還益州長史，未就道卒，年五十八，贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again returned as Chief Administrator of Yizhou but died before taking up the post, aged fifty-eight; posthumously made Prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as chief administrator of Yizhou but died before taking up the post at fifty-eight; he was posthumously made prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 味道練台閣故事，善占奏。

translations.literal: Weidao was versed in Secretariat precedents and skilled at memorials and reports.
translations.idiomatic: Weidao mastered Secretariat precedents and excelled at memorials and reports.

sentences.zh: 然其為相，特具位，未嘗有所發明，脂韋自營而已。

translations.literal: Yet as chief minister he merely filled the seat and never advanced anything of note, only greasing and currying favor for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as chief minister he merely occupied the seat, advanced no notable policies, and devoted himself only to self-preservation and flattery.

sentences.zh: 常謂人曰：「決事不欲明白，誤則有悔，摸棱持兩端可也。」

translations.literal: He often told people: "In deciding affairs one should not wish for clarity; if one errs there is regret—holding the edges and keeping both sides open will do.
translations.idiomatic: He often said: "Do not decide matters too clearly; mistakes bring regret. It is best to stay equivocal and keep both sides open.

sentences.zh: 故世號「摸棱手」。

translations.literal: Therefore the age called him "the equivocator."
translations.idiomatic: For this the age called him "the equivocator."

sentences.zh: 性友愛。

translations.literal: By nature he was affectionate toward kin.
translations.idiomatic: He was affectionate by nature.

sentences.zh: 其弟味元，味元嘗請托不遂，因慢折之，味道怡然不屑。

translations.literal: His younger brother Weiyuan—Weiyuan once made a request that was not granted and therefore treated him with contempt; Weidao remained calm and unconcerned.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Weiyuan, when a request went unfulfilled, treated him with contempt; Weidao remained calm and unperturbed.

sentences.zh: 所論著行于時。

translations.literal: His writings circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His writings circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 豆盧欽望豆盧欽望，雍州萬年人。

translations.literal: Doulu Qinwang — Doulu Qinwang, a man of Wannian in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Qinwang was a native of Wannian in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖寬，隋文帝外孫，為梁泉令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kuan was a grandson by marriage of Emperor Wen of Sui and served as magistrate of Liangquan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kuan, a grandson by marriage of Emperor Wen of Sui, served as magistrate of Liangquan.

sentences.zh: 高祖定關中，與郡守蕭瑀率豪姓進款。

translations.literal: When Gaozu secured Guanzhong, Kuan with the prefect Xiao Yu led powerful clans in submitting allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu secured Guanzhong, Kuan and the prefect Xiao Yu led the local magnates in submitting allegiance.

sentences.zh: 擢累殿中監。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to Director of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to director of the palace.

sentences.zh: 子懷讓，尚萬春公主。

translations.literal: His son Huairang married Princess Wanchun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huairang married Princess Wanchun.

sentences.zh: 詔寬用魏太和詔，去「豆」姓，著「盧」。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Kuan to follow the Northern Wei Taihe edict, drop the character "Dou" from the surname, and bear "Lu."
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Kuan, following the Northern Wei Taihe precedent, to drop the character Dou from the surname and bear Lu instead.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，遷禮部尚書、左衛大將軍，芮國公。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he was transferred to Minister of Rites and Great General of the Left Guard, Duke of Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenguan he became minister of rites and great general of the Left Guard, with the title Duke of Rui.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈特進、并州都督，陪葬昭陵，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Special Advance and Protector-General of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honors at Zhaoling, with posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made special advance and protector-general of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honors at Zhaoling, with the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 復其舊姓。

translations.literal: His original surname was restored.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was restored.

sentences.zh: 欽望累官越州都督、司賓卿。

translations.literal: Qinwang successively held the posts of Protector-General of Yuezhou and Director of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: Qinwang successively served as protector-general of Yuezhou and director of guests.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，拜內史，封芮國公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou he was appointed Inner Scribe and enfeoffed as Duke of Rui.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changshou he was appointed inner scribe and enfeoffed as Duke of Rui.

sentences.zh: 李昭德被罪，有司劾奏欽望阿順昭德不執正，附臣罔君，貶趙州刺史。

translations.literal: When Li Zhaode was charged with crimes, the relevant offices impeached Qinwang for fawning on Zhaode and failing to uphold rectitude, for a subject deceiving his ruler, and he was demoted to Prefect of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhaode was condemned, officials impeached Qinwang for flattering Zhaode instead of upholding justice and for deceiving the ruler; he was demoted to prefect of Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 入為司府卿，遷秋官尚書。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and was transferred to Minister of Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as director of the Court of the Imperial Clan and was promoted to minister of autumn.

sentences.zh: 中宗還東宮，拜太子宮尹。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong returned to the Eastern Palace, Qinwang was appointed Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzong returned to the Eastern Palace, Qinwang was appointed director of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 進文昌右相、同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: He advanced to Right Chancellor of the Secretariat and Third-Rank Associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right chancellor of the Secretariat and third-rank associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 罷為太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was dismissed and made Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed and made guest of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝復位，擢尚書左僕射、平章軍國重事。

translations.literal: When the emperor regained the throne, Qinwang was elevated to Left Vice-Director of the Department of State Affairs and given charge of weighty military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was restored to the throne, Qinwang was promoted to left vice-director of the Department of State Affairs with charge of weighty military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 欽望居宰相積十餘年，方易之、三思等怙勢宣烝，窺間王室，戮忠戚，觖冀非常，不能有所裁抑，獨謹身諄諄自全。

translations.literal: Qinwang served as chief minister for more than ten years while Yizhi, Sansi, and others relied on power to flaunt debauchery, watched for openings against the royal house, slaughtered loyal kin, and coveted extraordinary gains; he could not restrain them in any way and only guarded himself carefully, admonishing himself to survive.
translations.idiomatic: Qinwang served as chief minister for more than ten years while Yizhi, Sansi, and their faction abused power, eyed the throne, killed loyal princes and ministers, and pursued extravagant ambitions; he could not restrain them and devoted himself only to cautious self-preservation.

sentences.zh: 進開府儀同三司，檢校安國相王府長史。

translations.literal: He advanced to Grandee of the State with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies and acting Chief Administrator of the Anguo Prince of Xiang's household.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grandee of the state with ceremonial privileges equal to the Three Excellencies and made acting chief administrator of the Anguo Prince of Xiang's household.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十，贈司空、并州大都督，陪葬乾陵，諡曰元。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty, and was posthumously made Minister of Works and Grand Protector-General of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honors at Qianling, with posthumous title Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty and was posthumously made minister of works and grand protector-general of Bingzhou, buried with attendant honors at Qianling, with the posthumous name Yuan.

sentences.zh: 武后時，宰相又有史務滋、崔元綜、周允元，略可述者附左方。

translations.literal: In the time of Empress Wu there were also chief ministers Shi Wuzi, Cui Yuanzong, and Zhou Yun'yuan; those briefly worth recounting are appended below.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu there were also chief ministers Shi Wuzi, Cui Yuanzong, and Zhou Yun'yuan; brief accounts of those worth noting are appended below.

sentences.zh: 附 史務滋史務滋，宣州溧陽人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Shi Wuzi — Shi Wuzi, a man of Liyang in Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Shi Wuzi was a native of Liyang in Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 累吏勞，遷司賓卿，進拜納言。

translations.literal: Through accumulated service in clerical labor he was transferred to Director of Guests and advanced to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Through long service in administrative posts he rose to director of guests and then drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 後革命，詔務滋等十人分行天下。

translations.literal: After the dynastic revolution, an edict ordered Wuzi and nine others to travel the realm in separate circuits.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic revolution, an edict ordered Wuzi and nine others to tour the realm in separate circuits.

sentences.zh: 雅州刺史劉行實兄弟為侍御史來子珣誣其反，詔務滋與來俊臣雜治，俊臣言務滋與囚善，掩其反狀，後命俊臣並治，遂自殺。

translations.literal: The brothers Liu Xingshi and Liu Xingqi of Yazhou were slandered as rebels by the Attending Censor Lai Zixun; an edict ordered Wuzi and Lai Junchen to try the case jointly. Junchen said Wuzi was friendly with the prisoners and concealed their rebel evidence; later he was ordered to try Wuzi together with them, and Wuzi then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Liu brothers of Yazhou were framed for rebellion by attending censor Lai Zixun; Wuzi and Lai Junchen were ordered to try the case together. Junchen accused Wuzi of favoring the prisoners and concealing evidence of rebellion; when Wuzi was later placed under Junchen's jurisdiction as well, he committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 附 崔元綜崔元綜，鄭州新鄭人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Cui Yuanzong — Cui Yuanzong, a man of Xinzheng in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Cui Yuanzong was a native of Xinzheng in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖君肅，武德中為黃門侍郎、鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Junsu, during Wude, served as Vice-Director of the Yellow Gate and Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Junsu served under Wude as vice-director of the Yellow Gate and director of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 元綜，天授初以鸞台侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: Yuanzong, at the beginning of Tianshou, served as Vice-Director of the Crane Terrace and Associate Chief Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzong, at the start of the Tianshou era, served as vice-director of the Crane Terrace and associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 性恪慎，坐政事堂，束帶，終日不休偃，尤護細概。

translations.literal: By nature he was scrupulous and cautious; sitting in the Hall of Government Affairs he kept his belt fastened and never rested all day, especially guarding minute details.
translations.idiomatic: He was scrupulous by nature; in the Hall of Government Affairs he kept his belt fastened and never relaxed all day, guarding every minute detail.

sentences.zh: 外若謹厚，而中刻薄。

translations.literal: Outwardly he seemed careful and thick, but inwardly he was harsh and mean.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he seemed careful and generous, but inwardly he was harsh and mean.

sentences.zh: 每受制鞫獄，必澡垢索疵，不入死不肯止，人畏鄙之。

translations.literal: Whenever he received orders to interrogate cases, he always washed for dirt and sought flaws; unless the accused entered death he would not stop, and people feared and despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever ordered to interrogate a case, he hunted for every flaw and would not stop short of a death sentence; people feared and despised him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐事流振州，搢紳為慶。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of an offense he was banished to Zhenzhou, and the gentry rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was banished to Zhenzhou for an offense, to the relief of the gentry.

sentences.zh: 會赦還，除監察御史。

translations.literal: When an amnesty returned him, he was made Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After an amnesty brought him back, he was made investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 遷蒲州刺史，致仕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Puzhou and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Puzhou and then retired.

sentences.zh: 善攝生，年九十餘卒。

translations.literal: He was skilled at nurturing life and died aged more than ninety.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in nurturing his health, he died in his nineties.

sentences.zh: 附 周允元周允元字汝良，豫州安城人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Zhou Yun'yuan — Zhou Yun'yuan, style name Ruliang, a man of Ancheng in Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Zhou Yun'yuan, whose style name was Ruliang, was a native of Ancheng in Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 自右肅政御史中丞，拜檢校鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: From Censor-in-Chief of the Right Bureau for Rectifying Governance he was appointed Acting Vice-Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Associate Chief Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: From censor-in-chief of the Right Bureau for Rectifying Governance he was appointed acting vice-director of the Phoenix Pavilion and associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 武后宴宰相，詔陳書傳善言，允元曰：「恥其君不如堯、舜。」

translations.literal: When Empress Wu feasted the chief ministers, she ordered them to cite good words from the classics and histories; Yun'yuan said: "To feel shame that one's ruler is not like Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: At a feast for her chief ministers, Empress Wu asked them to cite worthy passages from the classics; Yun'yuan quoted: "To feel shame that one's ruler is not like Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 武三思劾奏語指斥，後曰：「聞其言足以誡，安得為過？」

translations.literal: Wu Sansi impeached him, saying the words were pointed rebuke; the Empress said: "Hearing his words is enough for admonition—how can this be a fault?"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi accused him of insolent rebuke, but the Empress replied: "His words are admonition enough—how can that be a fault?"

sentences.zh: 卒，贈貝州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made prefect of Beizhou.
